questions.sec: Paralytic squint — features and the CN III course
questions.q: Fill up: paralytic squint in the book is a type of ______ squint.
questions.exp: Paralytic squint is a type of incomitant squint. (Book p54)

questions.sec: Paralytic squint — features and the CN III course
questions.q: All of the following are listed features of paralytic squint in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Features: diplopia; abnormal head posture; restriction of ocular movements (intended action of the paralysed muscle — vertigo); deviation opposite to the action of the paralysed muscle; 2° deviation > 1° deviation. (Book p54)

questions.sec: Paralytic squint — features and the CN III course
questions.q: The deviation in paralytic squint per the book is ______ to the action of the paralysed muscle.
questions.exp: Deviation: opposite to the action of paralysed muscle. (Book p54)

questions.sec: Paralytic squint — features and the CN III course
questions.q: In paralytic squint per the book, the 2° deviation is ______ the 1° deviation.
questions.exp: 2° deviation > 1° deviation is a listed feature of paralytic squint. (Book p54)

questions.sec: Paralytic squint — features and the CN III course
questions.q: The cause of paralytic squint per the book is palsy of which nerves?
questions.exp: Cause: 3rd, 4th, 6th nerve palsy. (Book p54)

questions.sec: Paralytic squint — features and the CN III course
questions.q: The CN III nuclear complex is situated in the midbrain at the level of the:
questions.exp: Nuclear complex: situated in the mid-brain at level of superior colliculus. (Book p54)

questions.sec: Paralytic squint — features and the CN III course
questions.q: Match the CN III main motor nucleus subnucleus with its innervation in the book — 1) 2 paired subnuclei 2) 1 unpaired subnucleus … A) I/L MR, IR, IO and C/L SR B) Both LPS
opts: Both innervate I/L MR, IR, IO
questions.exp: Paired subnuclei innervate C/L SR and I/L MR, IR, IO; the unpaired subnucleus innervates both LPS; Edinger-Westphal (accessory nucleus) sends preganglionic parasympathetic fibres to sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle (constriction). (Book p54)

questions.sec: Paralytic squint — features and the CN III course
questions.q: Match the CN III segment with its course in the book — 1) Fascicular 2) Basilar 3) Intracavernous 4) Intraorbital … A) Superior division supplies LPS and SR; inferior division supplies IR, IO and MR B) Runs in the lateral wall above the trochlear nerve; divides into superior and inferior branches; enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure within the annulus of Zinn C) Fibres pass through the red nucleus into the interpeduncular D) Leaves the mid-brain on the medial aspect of the cerebral peduncle, between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries
questions.exp: Course: fascicular — fibres pass through red nucleus into interpeduncular; basilar — leaves the mid-brain on the medial aspect of the cerebral peduncle, between PCA and SCA; intracavernous — lateral wall above trochlear nerve, superior/inferior branches, enters orbit through superior orbital fissure within annulus of Zinn; intraorbital — superior division → LPS, SR; inferior division → IR, IO, MR. (Book p54)

questions.sec: CN III palsy — clinical features and special syndromes
questions.q: Match the muscle involved in CN III palsy with its clinical manifestation in the book's table — 1) LPS 2) Elevation group (SO/IR) 3) Medial rectus 4) Sphincter pupillae … A) Outward deviation: exotropia → crossed diplopia B) Ptosis (drooping of eyelid) C) Mydriasis with loss of pupillary light reflex D) Downward deviation: hypotropia
questions.exp: LPS — ptosis; SO/IR (elevation) — hypotropia (downward deviation); medial rectus — exotropia (outward deviation) → crossed diplopia; sphincter pupillae — mydriasis with loss of pupillary light reflex; ciliary muscle — loss of near vision/near reflex. (Book p55)

questions.sec: CN III palsy — clinical features and special syndromes
questions.q: Fill up: ciliary muscle paralysis in CN III palsy causes loss of near vision/near reflex, while sphincter pupillae paralysis causes ______ with loss of the pupillary light reflex.
questions.exp: Sphincter pupillae: normal miosis → mydriasis with loss of pupillary light reflex. (Book p55)

questions.sec: CN III palsy — clinical features and special syndromes
questions.q: The book's photo series of a left CN III palsy shows, in primary gaze:
opts: LE exotropia with a normal lid
LE ptosis + LE down and out
questions.exp: Primary gaze: LE ptosis + LE down and out; limited elevation of LE; limitation of adduction; down and outward movement present. (Book p55)

questions.sec: CN III palsy — clinical features and special syndromes
questions.q: Match the special CN III palsy syndrome with its lesion site/features in the book — 1) Benedikt's syndrome 2) Weber's syndrome 3) Nothnagel's syndrome … A) Cerebral peduncle — CN III palsy + C/L hemiparesis B) Red nucleus — CN III palsy + flapping tremors C) CN III palsy + cerebellar ataxia
questions.exp: Benedikt's: lesion at red nucleus, CN III palsy + flapping tremors; Weber's: lesion at cerebral peduncle, CN III palsy + C/L hemiparesis; Nothnagel's: CN III palsy + cerebellar ataxia. (Book p55)

questions.sec: CN III palsy — clinical features and special syndromes
questions.q: Daroff's rule for nuclear CN III palsy in the book lists all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Nuclear CN III palsy (Daroff's rule): B/L ptosis, C/L SR weakness, B/L mydriasis and cycloplegia. (Book p55)

questions.sec: CN III palsy — clinical features and special syndromes
questions.q: Which statement about the CN III palsy clinical features table is FALSE?
opts: Sphincter pupillae paralysis gives miosis with a preserved light reflex
Medial rectus paralysis gives exotropia with crossed diplopia
Ciliary muscle paralysis gives loss of near vision/near reflex
questions.exp: Sphincter pupillae paralysis gives MYDRIASIS with loss of the pupillary light reflex (not miosis). (Book p55)

questions.sec: CN III palsy — clinical features and special syndromes
questions.q: All of the following are listed under special clinical features of CN III palsy in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Special clinical features: vascular pathologies, uncal herniation, Benedikt's, Weber's, Nothnagel's, nuclear CN III palsy; Foville syndrome is a pons syndrome of CN VI palsy. (Book p55)

questions.sec: Vascular CN III palsy, treatment and aberrant regeneration
questions.q: Match the CN III fibre layer in the book's diagram with its supply/role — 1) Superficial fibres 2) Central deep fibres … A) Supplied by the vasa nervorum B) Supply the pupil (supplied by pial vessels)
questions.exp: Superficial fibres → pupil (pial vessel supply); central deep fibres — supplied by vasa nervorum. (Book p56)

questions.sec: Vascular CN III palsy, treatment and aberrant regeneration
questions.q: In uncal herniation per the book, only the ______ is paralysed, producing mydriasis only.
questions.exp: Uncal herniation: only sphincter pupillae paralysed → mydriasis only (superficial parasympathetic fibres compressed first). (Book p56)

questions.sec: Vascular CN III palsy, treatment and aberrant regeneration
questions.q: Which statement about vascular CN III palsy is FALSE per the book?
opts: It is caused by diabetes and hypertension
CN III palsy with pupillary sparing
questions.exp: Vascular pathologies (diabetes, hypertension): CN III palsy with pupillary SPARING; near reflex absent; light reflex spared (vasa nervorum affects central fibres, pupil fibres on the surface are pial-supplied). (Book p56)

questions.sec: Vascular CN III palsy, treatment and aberrant regeneration
questions.q: Per the book's treatment algorithm for paralytic squint, observation precedes surgery after ______ if no regeneration occurs.
questions.exp: Treatment: observation for 6 months (regeneration d/t neurolemma) → surgery if no regeneration occurs. (Book p56)

questions.sec: Vascular CN III palsy, treatment and aberrant regeneration
questions.q: Fill up: regeneration of the peripheral CN III occurs by the neurolemma formed by ______, while the CNS regenerates via oligodendrocytes.
questions.exp: Regeneration d/t neurolemma — CNS: oligodendrocytes; PNS: Schwann cells. (Book p56)

questions.sec: Vascular CN III palsy, treatment and aberrant regeneration
questions.q: Match the aberrant regeneration sign with its mechanism in the book — 1) Pseudo-von Graefe sign 2) Pseudo-Argyll Robertson pupil (ciliary muscle fibres supply the sphincter pupillae) … A) On downgaze both IR and LPS contract → depression of the eye + elevation of the upper lid → lid lag B) On near vision the ciliary muscle accommodates → sphincter miosis: accommodation reflex present
questions.exp: Pseudo-von Graefe: IR fibres start to supply LPS — on downgaze IR and LPS contract (eye depression + upper lid elevation) → lid lag (eyelid movement lags behind eyeball movement). Pseudo-ARP: ciliary fibres supply sphincter pupillae — near vision → miosis (accommodation reflex present); or sphincter fibres completely damaged → pupillary light reflex absent. (Book p56)

questions.sec: Vascular CN III palsy, treatment and aberrant regeneration
questions.q: Months after a CN III palsy, a patient's upper lid elevates on downgaze, producing lid lag. Per the book this pseudo-von Graefe sign is because fibres of the ______ have started to supply the LPS.
questions.exp: Pseudo-von Graffe sign: fibres of the IR start to supply the LPS — on downgaze both IR and LPS contract. (Book p56)

questions.sec: CN IV (trochlear) palsy — course and Park's 3-step test
questions.q: Fill up: CN IV palsy in the book is A/K/A ______ palsy.
questions.exp: IV cranial nerve palsy/trochlear nerve palsy: A/K/A superior oblique palsy; m/c congenital paralytic squint. (Book p57)

questions.sec: CN IV (trochlear) palsy — course and Park's 3-step test
questions.q: CN IV palsy per the book is the m/c ______ paralytic squint.
questions.exp: CN IV palsy: m/c congenital paralytic squint. (Book p57)

questions.sec: CN IV (trochlear) palsy — course and Park's 3-step test
questions.q: Match the CN IV segment with its course in the book — 1) Nucleus 2) Fascicular 3) Trunk 4) Cavernous 5) Intraorbital … A) Leaves the midbrain on the dorsal surface, between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries B) Curves around the aqueduct of sylvius and decussates C) Midbrain at the level of inferior colliculus D) Lateral wall between oculomotor and ophthalmic nerves; passes through the superior orbital fissure outside the annulus of Zinn E) Innervates the contralateral superior oblique
questions.exp: CN IV course: nucleus — midbrain at level of inferior colliculus; fascicular — curves around aqueduct of sylvius and decussates; trunk — leaves midbrain dorsally, between PCA and SCA; cavernous — lateral wall between oculomotor and ophthalmic nerves, through superior orbital fissure OUTSIDE the annulus of Zinn; intraorbital — innervates contralateral superior oblique. (Book p57)

questions.sec: CN IV (trochlear) palsy — course and Park's 3-step test
questions.q: Match the normal action of the SO with its manifestation on palsy in the book — 1) Intorsion 2) Depression 3) Depression in adduction … A) I/L hypertropia B) Outward rotation: excycloptropia C) ↑ Hypertropia on adduction, vertical diplopia on downgaze
questions.exp: Features are opposite to the action of the paralysed muscle: intorsion → excycloptropia (outward rotation); depression → I/L hypertropia; depression in adduction → ↑ hypertropia on adduction, vertical diplopia on downgaze. (Book p57)

questions.sec: CN IV (trochlear) palsy — course and Park's 3-step test
questions.q: Match the SO palsy manifestation with the patient's head posture in the book — 1) Excycloptropia 2) I/L hypertropia 3) Vertical diplopia on downgaze … A) Chin down B) Face turns to the opposite side C) Head tilt to the opposite side
questions.exp: Head posture: intorsion defect (excycloptropia) → head tilt to the opposite side; depression defect (I/L hypertropia) → chin down; depression-in-adduction defect (vertical diplopia on downgaze) → face turns to the opposite side. (Book p57)

questions.sec: CN IV (trochlear) palsy — course and Park's 3-step test
questions.q: Fill up: per the book's note, C/L hypertropia in trochlear palsy occurs only if the lesion is at the ______.
questions.exp: Note: C/L hypertropia occurs only if the lesion is at the nucleus (before decussation of the fascicle). (Book p57)

questions.sec: CN IV (trochlear) palsy — course and Park's 3-step test
questions.q: Match Park's 3-step test step for SO palsy with its finding in the book — 1) Step 1 2) Step 2 3) Step 3 … A) Hypertropia better on opposite tilt B) Hypertropia worse on opposite gaze C) Identification of hypertropia (LE)
questions.exp: Park's 3-step test: step 1 — identification of hypertropia (LE); step 2 — hypertropia worse on opposite gaze; step 3 — hypertropia better on opposite tilt. (Book p57)

questions.sec: CN IV (trochlear) palsy — course and Park's 3-step test
questions.q: The book's figure shows a left SO palsy: LE hypertropia is ↑ on right gaze and ↓ on right tilt (Bielschowsky head tilt). Park's 3-step test therefore implicates the:
questions.exp: LE hypertropia worse on right (opposite) gaze and better on right (opposite) tilt identifies the left superior oblique. (Book p57)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: To diagnose a cyclovertical muscle palsy (SR, IR, SO, IO) the book says to follow:
questions.exp: Note: cyclovertical muscle palsy (SR, IR, SO, IO) — to diagnose, follow Park's 3 step test. (Book p58)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: Match the Park's test step for cyclovertical palsy with its purpose in the book — 1) Step 1 2) Step 2 3) Step 3 … A) Identify muscles causing lateral gaze B) Identify muscles causing hypertropia C) Identify muscles causing head tilt
questions.exp: Park's 3 step test: 1. identify muscles causing hypertropia; 2. identify muscles causing lateral gaze; 3. identify muscles causing head tilt; the muscle implicated in all is the affected muscle. (Book p58)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: Fill up: in Park's test, the muscle implicated in hypertropia, lateral gaze worsening and head tilt is the ______ muscle.
questions.exp: The muscle implicated in all of the above (hypertropia, lateral gaze, head tilt) is the affected muscle. (Book p58)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: Match the CN VI segment with its course in the book — 1) Nucleus 2) Fascicular 3) Basilar 4) Intracavernous 5) Intraorbital … A) Pons, ventral to the floor of the 4th ventricle B) Leaves brainstem at the pontomedullary junction C) Enters the basilar cistern, crossed by the AICA, through Dorello canal into the cavernous sinus D) Runs inferomedially in the lateral wall in close relation to the ICA; enters orbit within the annulus of Zinn E) Innervates the ipsilateral lateral rectus
questions.exp: CN VI course: nucleus — pons, ventral to floor of 4th ventricle; fascicular — leaves brainstem at pontomedullary junction; basilar — basilar cistern, crossed by AICA, Dorello canal, cavernous sinus; intracavernous — inferomedial in lateral wall close to ICA, orbit within annulus of Zinn; intraorbital — ipsilateral lateral rectus. (Book p58)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: Match the cranial nerve nuclei with their location in the book's table — 1) III, IV 2) V, VI, VII, VIII 3) IX, X, XI, XII … A) Pons B) Midbrain C) Medulla
questions.exp: Nuclei of CN: III, IV — midbrain; V, VI, VII, VIII — pons; IX, X, XI, XII — medulla. (Book p58)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: Match the pons syndrome with its features in the book — 1) Foville syndrome 2) Millard-Gubler syndrome 3) Mobius syndrome … A) B/L 6/7 CN palsy B) I/L 5/6/7/8 CN palsy + central Horner's syndrome C) I/L 6/7 CN palsy + C/L hemiplegia
questions.exp: Syndromes affecting pons: Foville — I/L 5/6/7/8 CN palsy + central Horner's syndrome; Millard-Gubler — I/L 6/7 CN palsy + C/L hemiplegia; Mobius — B/L 6/7 CN palsy. (Book p58)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: All of the following are listed clinical features of CN VI palsy in the book EXCEPT:
opts: Limitation of abduction with inward deviation (LE esotropia)
questions.exp: CN VI palsy features: limitation of abduction → inward deviation (LE esotropia); diplopia — uncrossed type; I/L head posture; I/L horizontal gaze palsy. B/L severe visual loss is an arteritic AION feature. (Book p58)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: In the book's photo series of a left abducens nerve (CN VI) palsy, left gaze shows:
opts: Normal left gaze with right esotropia
questions.exp: Photo series: 1° gaze — LE esotropia; normal right gaze; left gaze — left abduction absent/limited. (Book p58)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: Fill up: limitation of abduction in CN VI palsy produces an inward deviation, i.e. ______.
questions.exp: Limitation of abduction → inward deviation (LE esotropia). (Book p58)

questions.sec: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
questions.q: In the book's CN VI course, the intracavernous segment runs in the lateral wall in close relation to the:
questions.exp: Intracavernous: runs inferomedially in the lateral wall, in close relation to ICA; enters orbit through superior orbital fissure within annulus of Zinn. (Book p58)

units.title: Paralytic squint — features and the CN III course
units.guide: Paralytic squint: a type of incomitant squint. Features: diplopia; abnormal head posture; restriction of ocular movements (intended action of the paralysed muscle — vertigo); deviation opposite to the action of the paralysed muscle; 2° deviation > 1° deviation. Cause: 3rd, 4th, 6th nerve palsy. CN III (oculomotor) course: nuclear complex in the midbrain at the level of the superior colliculus — main motor nucleus (2 paired subnuclei: C/L SR and I/L MR, IR, IO; 1 unpaired subnucleus: both LPS) + Edinger-Westphal accessory nucleus (preganglionic parasympathetic fibres to sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle — constriction). Fascicular: fibres pass through the red nucleus into the interpeduncular. Basilar: leaves the midbrain on the medial aspect of the cerebral peduncle, between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries. Intracavernous: lateral wall above the trochlear nerve; superior and inferior branches; enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure within the annulus of Zinn. Intraorbital: superior division → LPS, SR; inferior division → IR, IO, MR.

units.title: CN III palsy — clinical features and special syndromes
units.guide: Clinical features table: LPS (elevation of upper eyelid) → ptosis; SO/IR (elevation of eye) → hypotropia (downward deviation); medial rectus (adduction) → exotropia (outward deviation) → crossed diplopia; sphincter pupillae (miosis) → mydriasis with loss of pupillary light reflex; ciliary muscle (accommodation) → loss of near vision/near reflex. Photos: limited elevation of LE; primary gaze — LE ptosis + LE down and out; limitation of adduction; down and outward movement present. Special clinical features: vascular pathologies; uncal herniation; Benedikt's syndrome (red nucleus — CN III palsy + flapping tremors); Weber's syndrome (cerebral peduncle — CN III palsy + C/L hemiparesis); Nothnagel's syndrome (CN III palsy + cerebellar ataxia); nuclear CN III palsy — Daroff's rule: B/L ptosis, C/L SR weakness, B/L mydriasis and cycloplegia.

units.title: Vascular CN III palsy, treatment and aberrant regeneration
units.guide: CN III diagram: pial vessels supply the superficial fibres (→ pupil); central deep fibres supplied by the vasa nervorum. Uncal herniation: only sphincter pupillae paralysed → mydriasis only. Vascular pathologies: caused by diabetes, hypertension; CN III palsy with pupillary sparing, near reflex absent, light reflex spared. Treatment: observation 6 months (regeneration d/t neurolemma — CNS oligodendrocytes, PNS Schwann cells) → surgery if no regeneration. Faulty regeneration → aberrant regeneration: pseudo-von Graffe sign (IR fibres supply LPS — on downgaze IR and LPS contract → depression of eye + elevation of upper lid → lid lag); pseudo-Argyll Robertson pupil (ciliary fibres supply sphincter pupillae — near vision → accommodation miosis, accommodation reflex present; or sphincter fibres completely damaged → pupillary light reflex absent).

units.title: CN IV (trochlear) palsy — course and Park's 3-step test
units.guide: CN IV palsy: A/K/A superior oblique palsy; m/c congenital paralytic squint. Course: nucleus — midbrain at level of inferior colliculus; fascicular — curves around the aqueduct of sylvius and decussates; trunk — leaves the midbrain dorsally, between PCA and SCA; cavernous — lateral wall between oculomotor and ophthalmic nerves, through the superior orbital fissure OUTSIDE the annulus of Zinn; intraorbital — innervates the contralateral SO. Features (opposite to the paralysed action): intorsion → excycloptropia (head tilt to opposite side); depression → I/L hypertropia (chin down); depression in adduction → ↑ hypertropia on adduction, vertical diplopia on downgaze (face turns to opposite side). Note: C/L hypertropia only if the lesion is at the nucleus. Diagnosis — Park's 3-step test: step 1 identification of hypertropia (LE); step 2 hypertropia worse on opposite gaze; step 3 hypertropia better on opposite tilt (Bielschowsky head tilt).

units.title: Cyclovertical palsy note and CN VI (abducens) palsy
units.guide: Note: cyclovertical muscle palsy (SR, IR, SO, IO) — diagnose with Park's 3-step test: 1. muscles causing hypertropia; 2. muscles causing lateral gaze; 3. muscles causing head tilt; the muscle implicated in all is the affected muscle. CN VI (abducens/lateral rectus) palsy: nucleus — pons, ventral to floor of 4th ventricle; fascicular — leaves brainstem at the pontomedullary junction; basilar — basilar cistern, crossed by AICA, Dorello canal, cavernous sinus; intracavernous — inferomedial in the lateral wall close to the ICA, orbit within the annulus of Zinn; intraorbital — ipsilateral lateral rectus. CN nuclei locations: III/IV — midbrain; V, VI, VII, VIII — pons; IX-XII — medulla. Pons syndromes: Foville (I/L 5/6/7/8 CN palsy + central Horner's), Millard-Gubler (I/L 6/7 CN palsy + C/L hemiplegia), Mobius (B/L 6/7 CN palsy). Features: limitation of abduction → inward deviation (LE esotropia); diplopia — uncrossed; I/L head posture; I/L horizontal gaze palsy.
